title: Crawler-divide IMD replicates on seed 3 (12 persistent splits, gen 5, crawlers to 14.9 BL), but chi=0 still crawls 5.2 BL with crescents early
summary: Fresh seed 3 (founder position and kick): the founder crawls as a crescent, grows, pinches and separates; by t~240 there are ~12 crescent crawlers, which round up and freeze into a lattice of starving cells after t~350 (rerun/sheet.png). labkit: 12 persistent splits, max generation 5, merge/split 0.19; 17 tracks moved >= 1 BL, top 14.9, 12.3, 10.7, 9.5, 9.0 BL. chi=0 on the same seed: 16 persistent splits, generation 5, and still 16 tracks >= 1 BL, top 5.2, 4.3, 4.2 BL, with visible crescent crawlers at t=25-130 before jamming.

observations.I: rerun/sheet.png and rerun/tracks.png: discrete crescent cells, 15 at t=600
observations.M: rerun/metrics.json motion_top: 14.9, 12.3, 10.7 BL; crescents in rerun/sheet.png t=25-237
observations.D: rerun/lineage.png and FACTS.md: 12 persistent splits, generation 5, merge/split 0.19

controls_run.M: chi0/ (chi=0, seed 3): max 5.2 BL vs 14.9; crescents still move early

verdicts.limitation: The chi=0 control is weaker on this seed than claimed (5.2 BL vs <= 2.6), so chi raises motility about 3x rather than switching it on. Motility and division are confined to the food boom (t<~350); the population ends as a static lattice with no turnover. The author's own follow-ups (20261025T0908, 0917) show the regime depends on a content-independent growth drive from the finite-range term; this affects E-type interpretations, not the I, M, D observed here. Planted founder, so S does not apply; no dt or grid check.
